title: Wallets, transfers, USSD and bills: doing it right every time

say: Wallets, transfers, USSD and bills: doing it right every time.
This is the video for module 2 of Digital Payments and POS Basics.
A transfer takes less than a minute, but most mistakes happen in that minute. So you will learn a routine.

items: Check a wallet app before you trust it
Send a transfer with a routine
Pay without data, using USSD
Receive money without being tricked

say: You will also pay without internet, pay bills, and receive money safely.

say: Wallet apps like Opay, PalmPay and Moniepoint must be run by licensed companies. For example, Joy, a hairdresser in Port Harcourt, found two apps with the same logo, and chose the one whose publisher matched the company.
She found the licence statement, used her own number, set a strong PIN and saved support. No licence statement? Do not keep money there.

panel.heading: Five checks for any wallet app
items: Licence statement found
Publisher name matches the company
Registered with your own phone number
Strong PIN and app lock
Support channel saved

say: A message saying a supplier or school has a new account is a common trick. Confirm by calling the number you already have.
If you send to a wrong account, report it to your bank at once with the session ID.

say: USSD is a short code that starts with a star and ends with a hash. It works on any phone with signal, with no data. Get the code from your card or bank website.

panel.heading: Paying with no data
items: Get the code from your card or bank website
Use the SIM registered to your account
Write the details down before you dial
Check the name, then enter your USSD PIN

say: It only works with the SIM registered to your account. That is part of its security.

say: Every bill follows one pattern: service, number, amount, check, approve, keep proof.
For airtime, choose the network that matches the number, or it may go to a different number.

panel.heading: Check the number before you pay

cards.d: Choose the network that matches the phone number. Check every digit.
Enter the meter number exactly. Check the name shown. Type the 20-digit token into the meter.
Enter the smartcard or IUC number from the decoder. Keep it on to receive the update.

say: For prepaid electricity, enter your meter number exactly and check the name shown. The 20-digit token only works on that meter. If it is rejected, retype it slowly first.

panel.heading: Check the number before you pay

cards.d: Choose the network that matches the phone number. Check every digit.
Enter the meter number exactly. Check the name shown. Type the 20-digit token into the meter.
Enter the smartcard or IUC number from the decoder. Keep it on to receive the update.

say: For TV, enter the smartcard or IUC number and keep the decoder on. If a bill does not deliver, check your history first. Do not pay again.

say: Patience has 20,000 naira to spend on electricity this week.
The freezer uses most power, so she buys 12,000 for the shop. The name on screen matches, so she pays and saves the token.
Home gets the rest, 8,000. The name shown is her landlord's, as she expected.
20,000 in total, with two receipts and two tokens saved in case a meter rejects one.
For example, Aisha sells fabric in Ilorin. At closing, her notebook shows 6 transfer sales, 55,500 naira.
Her app history shows only 49,500. 6,000 is missing, from the woman who showed a screenshot when the stall was busy.
Release goods only when the credit is in your own app history.
Sometimes a caller says he sent you money by mistake, and asks you to send it back. Check your balance, not the SMS, and do not spend money you did not expect.

panel.heading: A mistaken credit
items: Check your balance, not the SMS
Do not spend money you did not expect
Report it to your bank's official support
Keep the complaint reference

say: Tell him to report it to his own bank. Report it to yours, and keep the reference. If the money is real, the banks will move it back. If the alert was fake, you have lost nothing.

panel.heading: A mistaken credit
items: Check your balance, not the SMS
Do not spend money you did not expect
Report it to your bank's official support
Keep the complaint reference
panel.rule: Never send a mistaken transfer back yourself.

say: To remember. Check the licence before trusting a wallet. Check the name, the number and the zeros before your PIN. Use USSD when data runs out. Check bill numbers before paying. And release goods only when the money shows in your own history.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Check the licence before trusting a wallet
Name, number in groups, amount, then PIN
USSD works without data, on your own SIM
Check meter or phone numbers before paying bills
Release goods only when the credit shows
